record.title: Nathan Tutorial
record.description:
We need a tutorial for Nathan. When players first get a Nathan token, that's when it will trigger the start of the FTUE specifically for Nathan

1. After they get their first Nathan token, we show them how to unlock
2. We then make them go to a pre level dialog, and show them how to change character on that dialog

Flow is something like:

1. User receives Nathan token
2. "Congrats, I think we have enough to unlock Nathan to help us on our journey, let's go to the character home"
3. "This is how you unlock a new character once you have collected enough tokens!"
4. "Nathan is now unlocked, let's return to our adventure and see what Nathan can do for us!"
5. Player gets redirected back to Saga map, we prompt a pre level dialog and we say "Oh oops, we forgot to actually bring Nathan along for the ride, we can quickly change characters here"
6. We show them how to change characters from pre-level dialog.
7. We make them play a level with Nathan
8. At beginning of that level, we highlight the streak bar and streak bonus icon on bottom and say "Remember, different characters have different abilities! Pay attention and see what Nathan can do!"

End tutorial.

record.title: Design Conveyor Belt Lore and Background
record.description:
Hey guys, some lore ideas for the minigames. I hope they can serve as a jumping point for us. Please give me your feedback and tell me what you think! ^^

Our mushroom village has residents that look like the Toad as a throwback to classic Mario series. These little tricksters can be seen carrying tiles to the river.

Since we’re aiming for a natural theme without any industrial elements we can skip lore for each mini game and have them appear in different sections of the game like rivers, clouds, forests, etc.

record.title: Tweak Puzzle Sequence Difficulty Using Symbol Weights
record.description:
Goal is to create two new tweakable parameters that can affect level difficulty:

1) Board pieces symbol frequency weights

2) Draw pieces symbol frequency weights

Documentation on symbol weights can be found [HERE]([URL_13532])

Conclusion:

Board pieces → Weighted, approximate distribution from most to least:

| 15.42% |
| 13.24% |
| 12.23% |
| 11.26% |
| 10.48% |
| 9.88% |
| 8.90% |
| 7.70% |
| 6.14% |
| 4.74% |

Draw pile pieces → Weighted, approximate distribution from most to least:

| 18.75% |
| 15.42% |
| 13.13% |
| 12.29% |
| 9.79% |
| 9.38% |
| 7.71% |
| 6.46% |
| 4.58% |
| 2.50% |

I propose we create a few levels using any level on the map to do the following level tests:

1. The weights of the draw pile matches the weights of the board pieces. With same weights on same symbols.
2. The weights of the draw pile matches the weights of the board pieces. With different weights on DIFFERENT symbols. Let's try the complete inverse, meaning the heaviest weighted board piece is the least weighted piece in the draw pile and so on…
3. The weights of the draw pile is equally random, 10% chance per symbol. ZERO weights.
4. The weights of the draw pile is more concentrated (more skewed) like it is in our data set, where the top frequency of the draw pile exceed those of the board. Matching symbols. We can maybe shift 20% of each weights to the heavier weights. So if A, B, C is 18%, 15%, 12%, then after weight shifted it A is now 18% + (15% \* 0.2) = 21%

   B is now 12% (3% went to A) + (12% \* 0.2) = 14.4%

   C is now 9.6% (2.4% went to B) + (D \* 0.2) = ….

   So on..
5. The weights of the draw pile is less concentrated, where the top frequency symbol in the draw pile is significantly lower than the frequency of that same symbol in the board pieces. Same as #4 but shift everything to the right by 20%.

record.title: Create Test Levels For Object Composition
record.description:
We want to test the current resize on tap area logic. 

1. Creating a range of Unity primitives based on tap real estate on the board
   (Baseline range)
2. Levels where primitives and resembling objects are side by side 
   (Perceptual consistency evaluation)
3. Levels with multiple primitives and multiple resembling objects side by side. 
   (Real-world scaling composition evaluation)
   
   
   Branch Active: [PERSON_NAME_0019]/itemcompositiontest
   
   Task 1: Decide Min-Max Threshold 
   
   We need to decide what's the smallest and largest tap area we allow players on an object from a difficulty and aesthetics standpoint. 
   
   a. Minimum First 
   
   The minimum tap area should be visible on the screen. If levels are made out of the smallest tap area objects, it shouldn't look absurd. And it should still be clickable comfortably. 
   
   b. Maximum Second
   
   The max is more straightforward. It shouldn't be big enough that the object looks too out of place especially compared to the decided small item. Think sheriff bagde vs couch. 
   
   To help decide, these are the test levels (unchecked for prod)
   
   1. CylinderMinTapArea
   
   Shows beer mugs (bulky cylinder) with 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, and 0.35 script sizing. 
   
   2. BadgeMinTapArea
   
    Show badges (flat small) with 0.25, 0.275, and 0.3 script sizing. 

      3\. RakeMinTapArea

      Rakes in different colors, 0.5,0.6, and 0.7 in script sizing. 

      4\. BeerMaxTap
      
 Beers in different sizes 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 in script sizing and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison    and perceptual consistency.

5. CouchMaxTap
   
   This is the bulkiest object so it's the ultimate threshold for maximum tap area. This level has couch script sizes 0.75, 0.85, and 0.95 and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison.

Task 2: Decide shape categories (prefab sizing among peers)

Every item gets a shape label according to these categories 

1. Narrow Vertical (fork, pen, wine bottle, billiard stick)
2. Flat (chocolate, plate, pizza box, badge, music note, letters)
3. Bulky Polygon (gift box, washing machine, barrel)
4. Bulky Wide (couch, fridge, bicycle)
5. Tall Irregular (lamp, plunger)


Task 3: Define global min and max for each shape

1. For example the smallest narrow vertical item we will have in the game is a "rake"
2. The smallest flat item we will have in the game is "badge"

Task 4: Resize things accordingly.

Don't over adjust

record.title: Zombie Ops #2 Spec (Brain Chase)
record.description:
This the collectibles-based LiveOps event, aka **zombie version of Win and Collect.** Working title is Brain Chase with the alternate event name Serum Therapy. 

Here are some brain storm jump points for when we are ready to tackle this spec. 

* Collectible ideas: brains, tombstones, serums, worms, spiders (cute edition)
  
  Iteration idea: If we go with worms and spiders, we can make them moving so player feels like "catching" them. Adds to the fun and replays the same emotion in Royal Match where moving blocks of the collectible affects the collectible state. 


* Brain Chase is a time-limited event consisting of several steps. Each step has its collectible item goal and reward. You collect the items within the level by just tapping them while playing a level.
  
  Alternative: We can make it a match 3 to get the collectible item to keep it dynamic, similar to how you have to make a propeller in Royal Match to keep the mechanic one step above the mere collect.
   
* When players collect the item goal of a step, they need to finish the level to claim it. Thus, extra collectibles for hard and epic levels. 
  
  Alternative: Multiply rewards with rewarded ad? 
* The event has progression within itself. When you complete all steps in the event, you win the Grand Prize.
* Some name ideas: Brain Chase, Serum Therapy, Ghoul Goals, Zombie Zing, Graveyard Dash

record.description:
![image.png]([URL_52355])

Figma Link: [https://www.figma.com/design/TvRw8na5iGd3NynbSRUGFy/Zombie-Match-3D?node-id=782-2&p=f&t=VRKdThpBQWvZBKD4-0](https://www.figma.com/design/TvRw8na5iGd3NynbSRUGFy/Zombie-Match-3D?node-id=782-2&p=f&t=VRKdThpBQWvZBKD4-0)


We need a **short, snappy 2D animation** for the Weekly Contest reward screen. The animation should bring the purple reward chest to life in a way that feels satisfying and rewarding, but **fast-paced and skippable**. 

The animation leads into the **reward icon reveal** (handled separately in development). So, we need to account for that when deciding the timing of the box opening animation. 

Guidelines:

* You can decide the animation direction. Both opening up and sliding to the side are acceptable. But I think a small wobble followed by a generic opening upward is the most satisfying. 
* Animation should be **no longer than 0.5-1 second,** since we need to spare time for the icon reveal, as well. The whole scene should take more than 2 seconds. 
* Motion should be **clean and sharp**— let's avoid floaty easing or long anticipation.
* This part of the animation should support being **interruptible** without breaking the icon reveal and claim flow, **just in case** we decide to add a skipping /freezing later.
  without breaking the claim flow.
* Please use **simple VFX flourishes** as needed (light burst, sparkles), but keep it aligned with our current visual style.

record.title: Create Test Levels For Object Composition
record.description:
We want to test the current resize on tap area logic. 

1. Creating a range of Unity primitives based on tap real estate on the board
   (Baseline range)
2. Levels where primitives and resembling objects are side by side 
   (Perceptual consistency evaluation)
3. Levels with multiple primitives and multiple resembling objects side by side. 
   (Real-world scaling composition evaluation)
   
   
   Branch Active: [PERSON_NAME_0019]/itemcompositiontest
   
   Task 1: Decide Min-Max Threshold 
   
   We need to decide what's the smallest and largest tap area we allow players on an object from a difficulty and aesthetics standpoint. 
   
   a. Minimum First 
   
   The minimum tap area should be visible on the screen. If levels are made out of the smallest tap area objects, it shouldn't look absurd. And it should still be clickable comfortably. 
   
   b. Maximum Second
   
   The max is more straightforward. It shouldn't be big enough that the object looks too out of place especially compared to the decided small item. Think sheriff bagde vs couch. 
   
   To help decide, these are the test levels (unchecked for prod)
   
   1. CylinderMinTapArea
   
   Shows beer mugs (bulky cylinder) with 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, and 0.35 script sizing. 
   
   2. BadgeMinTapArea
   
    Show badges (flat small) with 0.25, 0.275, and 0.3 script sizing. 

      3\. RakeMinTapArea

      Rakes in different colors, 0.5,0.6, and 0.7 in script sizing. 

      4\. BeerMaxTap
      
 Beers in different sizes 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 in script sizing and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison    and perceptual consistency.

5. CouchMaxTap
   
   This is the bulkiest object so it's the ultimate threshold for maximum tap area. This level has couch script sizes 0.75, 0.85, and 0.95 and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison.

Task 2: Decide shape categories (prefab sizing among peers)

Every item gets a shape label according to these categories 

1. Narrow Vertical (fork, pen, wine bottle, billiard stick)
2. Flat (chocolate, plate, pizza box, badge, music note, letters)
3. Bulky Polygon (gift box, washing machine, barrel)
4. Bulky Wide (couch, fridge, bicycle)
5. Tall Irregular (lamp, plunger)


Task 3: Define global min and max for each shape

1. For example the smallest narrow vertical item we will have in the game is a "rake"
2. The smallest flat item we will have in the game is "badge"

Task 4: Resize things accordingly.

Don't over adjust

record.title: Zombie Ops #2 Spec (Brain Chase)
record.description:
This the collectibles-based LiveOps event, aka **zombie version of Win and Collect.** Working title is Brain Chase with the alternate event name Serum Therapy. 

Here are some brain storm jump points for when we are ready to tackle this spec. 

* Collectible ideas: brains, tombstones, serums, worms, spiders (cute edition)
  
  Iteration idea: If we go with worms and spiders, we can make them moving so player feels like "catching" them. Adds to the fun and replays the same emotion in Royal Match where moving blocks of the collectible affects the collectible state. 


* Brain Chase is a time-limited event consisting of several steps. Each step has its collectible item goal and reward. You collect the items within the level by just tapping them while playing a level.
  
  Alternative: We can make it a match 3 to get the collectible item to keep it dynamic, similar to how you have to make a propeller in Royal Match to keep the mechanic one step above the mere collect.
   
* When players collect the item goal of a step, they need to finish the level to claim it. Thus, extra collectibles for hard and epic levels. 
  
  Alternative: Multiply rewards with rewarded ad? 
* The event has progression within itself. When you complete all steps in the event, you win the Grand Prize.
* Some name ideas: Brain Chase, Serum Therapy, Ghoul Goals, Zombie Zing, Graveyard Dash

record.title: Zombie Gamemode #1 Spec (Operation: No Exit) "Endless Mode"
record.description:
We are going to add an "Endless Mode" as the first game mode of Zombie Match 3D. Working title is Operation: No Exit. 

Alternate names: Forever Brains, Till Death Loops Us Apart, Last Zom Standing, Match ‘Em Dead

There isn't a lot of art need for this one, just simple pre-level dialogue UIs and perhaps a few differentiators for the level. 

Some brain storm jump points. 

Mechanic #1 Item Dump 

If we want to make the endless mode more about matching, we can go an item dump to the board in fixed intervals. That way, there is a clear fail condition to end the endless of the endless mode and players can be scored based on how long they survived. If the board gets full beyond allowed capacity, we fail. Extra hard if each item dump has different items. 

Pros: Perfect for the match-oriented players. 
Cons: Can get frustrating very quickly. 

Mechanic #2 Zombie Difficulty

If we want to focus on zombie killing aspect to engage the players, we can opt for giving players ammunition of the same item set and weapon items to make them carrots on the otherwise repetitive mode. The zombie waves get progressively harder and if they reach the cannon; it's game over. 

Pros: Has flow, momentum, and possibility to help players zone out with repetitive action. 
Cons: If the player is more of a "matcher", they won't find it challenging enough because zombies won't do much for them.

1. Shooting board with a zombie head nailed on it by an axe (complete reuse of assets if we're on a crunch), or an arrow. 
2. An icon based on a theme: brain, cannonball, tombstone. Anything to replace the helmet of Helmet Rush.   
3. Multipliers come with evolving icons. For example, a humble cross tombstone for x1 and a full crypt for x10. Or military officer ranks based on our main hero.

record.title: Make The New Winstreak Adjustments
record.description:
Previously we had two winstreak rewards, the glue bucket and the trampoline. Now these will change into a rocket and an hourglass. 


![image.png]([URL_52988])

1. The winstreak is still capped at 5. 
2. Players get rockets and hourglasses in their pile based on their winstreak level (this rule is already in place). For example, if they have 3/5 winstreak, they start the level with 3 hourglasses and 3 rockets in their pile. 
3. If player clicks the hourglass, it adds **12 seconds** to the timer in the level. This number can change so please expose the value in the editor. 

![image.png]([URL_52987])

4 If the timer comes from the select booster portion, it gives 30 seconds instead. 

5. If the player clicks the rocket, 3 more rockets come out of it and make a match instead of the player. See the Match Factory reference here: 
   
   [[URL_52986])
   
   If there is only a single set of items remaining in the level, and the rocket doesn't get clicked by that point, it becomes unclickable. 

6. If players click on either the hourglass or the rocket under "select boosters" section, these boosters apply automatically at level start. 

Note: The UI is currently in progress. When that changes I will add a Figma link here. But they will in the same "Lite" page on Figma with everything else.
